headline: High-risk shared-write orchestration: default configs enable prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors across Kestra and LangGraph.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write shared files and stdin/stdout, and LangGraph can pass application-defined files and developer-defined tool outputs through graph state. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent consumes the other's artifacts or messages. No MCP/shared clipboard is shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Kestra outputs workflow artifacts that LangGraph later parses as instructions or tool arguments
IF both agents are pointed at the same application-defined workspace or storage path
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter/schema between artifacts and prompts
Require provenance tags on all cross-agent messages
Disable automatic parsing of free-form file contents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while LangGraph handles model-provider API keys and graph state. Both have broad network egress and filesystem access, so sensitive data can flow from Kestra into LangGraph outputs or provider calls in default deployments. The shared workspace risk is enough to treat leakage as high.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows place database data, cloud storage data, or logs into shared graph state
IF LangGraph nodes forward that state to model providers or developer-defined tools
mitigations: Remove secrets and PII before handoff
Restrict outbound destinations for both agents
Store API keys in a separate secret manager

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files, execute shell commands, and spawn subprocesses; Kestra also requests root/docker.sock, while LangGraph supports multiple instances with shared state via a checkpointer store. If they operate on the same mutable workspace or state backend, concurrent writes and state corruption are plausible by default and can be irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, database, or checkpointer store
IF Kestra runs with the requested elevated privileges while LangGraph instances are concurrent
mitigations: Run one agent at a time for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra produces workflow outputs, logs, and notifications; LangGraph is a stateful agent framework whose nodes may act on prior node outputs. If LangGraph treats Kestra outputs as authoritative, an upstream mistake can cascade into downstream actions like API calls, emails, or tool execution. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF LangGraph consumes Kestra-generated artifacts without an explicit verification step
IF downstream LangGraph nodes can send emails, call APIs, or trigger tools based on those artifacts
mitigations: Insert a human review gate before action nodes
Require checksum or schema validation on Kestra outputs
Mark Kestra outputs as untrusted by default

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra explicitly touches logs, messages, notifications, database data, and cloud storage data, while LangGraph handles graph state and model-provider API keys. The profiles do not state residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because uncertainty escalates, medium is appropriate rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Kestra workflows and then persisted in LangGraph checkpointer storage
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two deployment environments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared state
